summary: A Happier Couples / Sex with Dr. Jess podcast episode (May 26, 2022) on masochism and the pleasure of pain, hosted by Jess O'Reilly and Brandon Ware with guest Leigh Cowart, a researcher and journalist. Cowart discusses her book Hurts So Good: The Science and Culture of Pain on Purpose, her ballet background and recovery, the subjectivity of pain, consent, the line between safe indulgence and self-harm, and the role of pain in meaning and ritual. The episode also includes a sponsor promotion for oral sex courses and mention of FDA-approved Laurels underwear. The transcript ends mid-sentence while discussing the origin of the word masochism.
one_line: Podcast episode with researcher Leigh Cowart on masochism, consensual pain, consent, and her book Hurts So Good.
key_facts: The episode was published May 26, 2022 and runs 36:42 as a Happier Couples / Sex with Dr. Jess podcast.
Guest Leigh Cowart is a researcher and journalist whose latest book is Hurts So Good: The Science and Culture of Pain on Purpose.
Cowart describes the book as being about all the ways humans consent to feeling bad, to feel better.
Cowart started ballet at age four and danced professionally until her early twenties, describing the training as very abusive.
Cowart said she had a near lethal eating disorder from her time in ballet.
Cowart defines masochism as the deliberate act of choosing to feel bad, to feel better.
Cowart states that masochism requires consent without question, and that if you cannot opt out of suffering it is not masochism.
Cowart's example of pain researcher Dr. Lawmore involves a stick that he mistook for an Eastern Brown snake bite, illustrating that pain is subjective and shaped by context and expectation.
Cowart says the line between safe play and self-harm is always moving, and asks whether play feels compulsive or whether one can say no.
Cowart notes the word masochism came from psychopathic sexuality, one of the first European texts about sexual pathology.
Cowart cites the 2014 Ice Bucket Challenge for ALS as an example of suffering increasing perceived value of an outcome.
Cowart mentions Taboo trade shows across Canada, with dungeon areas for newcomers, in cities including Halifax, Montreal, Toronto, Calgary and Edmonton.
Cowart suggests starter questions: where masochism already shows up in your life, what areas you are curious about, how to explore them, and how to talk with partners.
The episode promoted 25% off Mind-Blowing oral courses at HappierCouples.com with code PODCAST.
Co-host Brandon Ware announced that Laurels underwear was approved by the FDA for safer oral sex.
